title: Microbatch conflation and epoch snapshot coordinator to reduce kernel churn and stabilize KV warmup
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Problem: The continuous batcher currently emits many small kernel executions during low-latency tails. Each micro-batch forces a kernel startup and a KV cache reconciliation pass, which together increase CPU jitter and cause frequent KV snapshot churn on busy hosts. This contributes to higher p99 latency and variable GPU occupancy.

Goal: Implement a microbatch conflation layer that opportunistically merges adjacent microbatches into a single kernel invocation within a bounded time/size budget, and introduce an epoch-based snapshot coordinator for KV cache warmup/eviction that removes global locks and reduces snapshot thrash. This work should be low-risk, backward-compatible, and instrumented for rollout with feature flags and telemetry.

Why now: Ongoing latency regressions in canary clusters (see dashboard) are traced to high kernel launch counts and repeated KV snapshot writes during model swaps. This refactor targets immediate p95/p99 improvement with minimal changes to public API or customer-visible behavior.
updates: 2026-03-10: RFC drafted and shared with runtime team. Proposed conflation algorithm uses a 1.5ms micro-window with a max merge size of 32 tokens per conflation unit. Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Microbatch+Conflation+RFC

2026-03-11: Spike implemented to validate merge correctness with streaming callers. Local perf run (nvprof) showed ~18% reduction in kernel launches for mixed short/medium sequences. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1823

2026-03-12: Design review with Marcus, Priya, and Omar. Decision: keep conflation decision in admission path (not executor) to preserve per-tenant QOS. Agreed to expose a runtime flag 'conflation.window_ms' and a per-tenant hard cap. Added lightweight metric: runtime.conflation.merged_batches and runtime.conflation.drop_reasons

2026-03-13: Prototype of epoch snapshot coordinator completed. Coordinator batches KV snapshot requests into epoch frames to avoid duplicate writes during rapid warmups. Integration test added. Observability hooks added to snapshot.trace and slot. Marked as In Progress and gating on two PRs merging.
comments: Priya Nair (2026-03-11): Nice spike. Please ensure streaming latency for one-token streaming doesn't regress — add microbench that measures token-level tail latency.

Omar Singh (2026-03-12): We should avoid introducing cross-shard coordination in hot paths; epoch coordinator must be local-first with async reconciliation. Consider using a weakly-consistent lease instead of global barriers.
Marcus Holt (2026-03-12): Approved prototype plan. Follow-ups: add chaos tests for model-swap during conflation and a canary rollout plan with rollback signal on error budget increase.

Security (2026-03-12): KV snapshot coordinator touches disk checkpoints. Confirm no PII is written and that KMS encryption is respected in snapshot path. Action: add unit that asserts encryption metadata present.
links: Incident writeup (root cause traced to kernel churn): https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-0123-kernel-churn
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: runtime.conflation.merged_batches and runtime.snapshot.epoch_frames available in console
Performance: canary shows >=10% reduction in kernel launches and >=5% improvement in p99 for mixed short-seq workloads vs baseline
Correctness: no change in model output ordering or token duplication for streaming clients
Stability: KV snapshot I/O volume during model swap reduced by >=40% in integration test harness
Rollout: feature gated behind 'conflation.enabled' with automated rollback if error budget increases
implementation_notes: Key components: 1) Admission conflation buffer with time-based flush (1-5ms tunable) and size cap; 2) Epoch snapshot coordinator that groups snapshot requests into frame ids and performs async reconcile without blocking request path; 3) Telemetry and feature flags with per-tenant overrides. Avoid global locks: use shard-local epoch counters and lightweight compare-and-swap for coordinator leadership. Keep snapshot write format unchanged to remain compatible with existing restore tooling.
testing_plan: Unit tests for conflation correctness (ordering, dropout, partial flush), integration test for model-swap warmup under load, chaos test that kills executor threads during conflation to ensure graceful fallback, canary rollout to 3% traffic with staged ramps and automated dashboard checks (latency, errors, kernel launches). Add perf microbench for one-token streaming latency and token-per-second throughput.
risks:
- Conflation could increase tail latency for extremely low-latency streaming use-cases if misconfigured.
- Snapshot coordinator introduces additional async paths; bugs could delay warmup and increase cold-start.
- Dependency bump (libaio -> 0.4.0 and tokio upgrade) required for async flush paths; these carry risk and are tracked in separate PRs.
followups: ENG-314271: follow up to port prefetch state machine to new coordinator hooks
ENG-271828: admission token migration task to align with new conflation admission counters
